title: Larimar Therapeutics Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial and Business Update
summary: Positive longer-term open label study data further demonstrated nomlabofusp's well-characterized safety profile, sustained increases in skin frataxin levels, and continued improvements in key clinical outcome measures High patient and investigator enthusiasm continues with additional participants
body_text: Larimar Therapeutics Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial and Business Update PDF Version August 4, 2026 at 7:00 AM EDT Positive longer-term open label study data further demonstrated nomlabofusp's well-characterized safety profile, sustained increases in skin frataxin levels, and continued improvements in key clinical outcome measures High patient and investigator enthusiasm continues with additional participants in the OL study dosed in July and several adults and adolescents in screening as of month-end Rolling BLA submission seeking accelerated approval underway, with the first module submitted and completion expected 2H 2026 Dosing of first patient in global confirmatory Phase 3 study expected Q3 2026 $156.3 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities as of June 30, 2026, with projected cash runway into the third quarter of 2027 BALA CYNWYD, Pa., Aug. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Larimar Therapeutics, Inc. (Larimar) (Nasdaq: LRMR), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing treatments for complex rare diseases, today reported its second quarter 2026 operating and financial results. “This is a defining period for Larimar as we advance nomlabofusp toward potential approval, supported by a clear path to submission, a robust data package, and continued clinical momentum,” said Carole Ben-Maimon, MD, President and Chief Executive Officer of Larimar. “Open label (OL) study data announced in June further reinforce the disease-modifying potential of nomlabofusp, demonstrating continued directional improvements in key clinical endpoints over time alongside a well-characterized safety profile. Following receipt of minutes from a successful Type B multidisciplinary pre-BLA meeting with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the first module of our rolling Biologics License Application (BLA) has been submitted, with completion expected in the second half of 2026. We continue to see strong enthusiasm from patients and investigators as we advance the OL study with additional participants dosed in July and several adults and adolescents in screening. We are also on track to initiate dosing in our global confirmatory study this quarter. Looking ahead, we are focused on execution as we work to bring forward nomlabofusp as the first potential therapy to address the underlying cause of disease for pediatric and adult patients living with Friedreich’s ataxia (FA).” Highlights June Open Label Study Data Release. As of June 2026, 43 adolescent and adult participants in the OL study received at least one dose of nomlabofusp and 22 participants remain in the study with a maximum treatment duration of more than 800 days. More than 10,000 doses of nomlabofusp have been administered. Consistent Long-term Safety Profile . Longer-term dosing was generally well tolerated with thirteen adults on treatment for one year, seven for 18 months and three for two years. The most common adverse events remained mild-to-moderate local injection site reactions, which decreased in frequency over time and did not lead to any withdrawals from the study. Twenty-one participants discontinued since study initiation in January 2024. Ten participants experienced anaphylaxis and discontinued the study, including nine participants with prior nomlabofusp exposure; all participants who experienced anaphylaxis responded to standard therapy and all returned to their usual state of health with no further sequelae. Three participants experienced generalized urticaria and discontinued the study, with no new occurrences observed following initiation of antihistamine therapy. Other discontinuations included three associated with other adverse events and five discontinuations unrelated to treatment, primarily due to logistical factors. Of the eleven participants who had previously not been exposed to nomlabofusp, one had anaphylaxis. Sustained Increases in Skin FXN Levels Comparable to Asymptomatic Carriers . Skin frataxin (FXN) levels increased following nomlabofusp administration, with 82% (9/11) of participants achieving levels above those in asymptomatic carriers by six months, 100% (9/9) reaching this threshold at one year, and 100% (3/3) maintaining it through 18 months. Improvements in Key Clinical Outcome Measures Relative to FACOMS Natural History Population . Directional improvement across key clinical endpoints, including mFARS, FARS-ADL, and 9-HPT1, was sustained following one year of nomlabofusp treatment (n=13) relative to a worsening in those outcomes observed in the Friedreich’s Ataxia Clinical Outcome Measures Study (FACOMS) reference population. Nomlabofusp led to a 2.6-point benefit in mFARS at one year. Improvement in clinical outcomes was associated with increased skin FXN levels, supporting the potential for nomlabofusp to provide clinical benefit across a broad spectrum of patients with FA, including those with advanced disease. 1Modified Friedreich Ataxia Rating Scale (mFARS), FARS-Activities of Daily Living (FARS-ADL), 9-hole peg test (9-HPT) FDA Alignment on BLA Submission Following Multidisciplinary Type B Pre-BLA Meeting: In June, following minutes from a multidisciplinary Type B pre-BLA meeting and FDA review of the nomlabofusp briefing package, Larimar announced continued agreement with the FDA on key elements of a potential BLA submission including: Sufficient Data Package: FDA confirmed that the existing data package appears capable of supporting submission and review of a BLA seeking accelerated approval based on data from the OL study; approval will be a matter of review. FXN as a Novel Surrogate Endpoint: FDA reaffirmed its willingness to consider FXN as a novel surrogate endpoint and confirmed that Larimar's exposure-response analysis linking nomlabofusp exposure to clinical outcomes may support the BLA submission. Gene Expression and Lipid Biomarkers: FDA stated that the prospectively collected gene expression and lipid biomarker data may provide an opportunity to further characterize the biological activity of nomlabofusp beyond FXN tissue concentrations. Rolling BLA Submission: FDA agreed to a rolling BLA submission. Rolling BLA Initiated. In June, Larimar submitted the first module of its rolling BLA submission seeking accelerated approval. Ongoing Advancement of OL Study . As of the end of July, additional participants received their initial dose with several adults and adolescents currently in screening. Upcoming Milestones Global Confirmatory Phase 3 Study: Dosing of first patient expected Q3 2026. Rolling BLA Submission: Completion expected 2H 2026 of submission seeking accelerated approval. Launch Timing: Targeting mid-2027 launch, if approved. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results As of June 30, 2026, the Company had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaling $156.3 million. The Company projects its cash runway into the third quarter of 2027. Second quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2025 The Company reported a net loss for the second quarter of 2026 of $32.8 million, or $0.30 per common share, compared to a net loss of $26.2 million, or $0.41 per common share, for the second quarter of 2025. Research and development expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $28.0 million compared to $23.4 million for the second quarter of 2025. The increase in research and development expenses was primarily driven by a $2.2 million increase in process performance qualification, and other drug manufacturing activities at our third-party manufacturers and a $2.0 million increase in professional and consulting fees associated with our ongoing and planned clinical trials, data analysis costs, FDA inspection readiness expenditures, as well as BLA preparation costs. General and administrative expenses were $6.4 million in the second quarter of 2026 compared to $4.4 million in the second quarter of 2025. The increase in general and administrative expenses primarily related to the acceleration of commercial activities as we prepare for the planned mid-2027 launch of nomlabofusp, if approved. This included an increase of $0.7 million of increased compensation costs associated with additional commercial and related headcount, an increase of $0.5 million of market development activities and commercial readiness efforts as well as an increase of $0.5 million in legal fees supporting commercialization and development efforts. Six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the six months ended June 30, 2025 The Company reported a net loss for the first six months of 2026 of $62.4 million, or $0.61 per common share, compared to a net loss of $55.5 million, or $0.87 per common share, for the first six months of 2025. Research and development expenses for the six months ended June 30, 2026, were $53.0 million compared to $49.9 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. This increase was driven by a $3.7 million increase in professional and consulting fees associated with our ongoing and planned clinical trials, data analysis costs, inspection readiness expenditures as well as BLA preparation costs partially offset by lower manufacturing activities and there related costs in the six month period ended June 30, 2026 compared to the six month period ended June 30, 2026. General and administrative expenses were $12.4 million for the first six months of 2026 compared to $9.1 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The increase in general and administrative expenses primarily related to the acceleration of commercial activities as we prepare for the planned mid-2027 launch of nomlabofusp, if approved. This included an increase of $1.6 million in market research, market development and other commercial readiness activities, an increase of $1.0 million of increased compensation costs associated with additional commercial and related headcount, as well as an increase of $0.5 million in legal fees supporting commercialization and development efforts. Larimar’s lead compound, nomlabofusp, is being developed as a potential treatment for Friedreich's ataxia. Larimar also plans to use its intracellular delivery platform to design other fusion proteins to target additional rare diseases characterized by deficiencies in intracellular bioactive compounds. title: KabaFusion Selects CareCloud to Build First-of-Its-Kind Platform for Home Infusion and Specialty Pharmacy
summary: KabaFusion partners with CareCloud to develop a fully integrated application, powered by artificial intelligence, designed for the home infusion workflow ...
body_text: KabaFusion partners with CareCloud to develop a fully integrated application, powered by artificial intelligence, designed for the home infusion workflow Somerset, NJ and Lexington, MA, Aug. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- KabaFusion, one of the nation's largest providers of home infusion therapy, and CareCloud, Inc. (Nasdaq: CCLD) (“CareCloud” or the “Company”), a leader in healthcare technology, today announced a partnership to build LailaCare, a platform powered by artificial intelligence and designed to support and modernize KabaFusion's operations as a home infusion and specialty pharmacy provider. CareCloud will design and develop the platform, which will be owned by KabaFusion. LailaCare will unify workflows including referral intake, eligibility and authorization, patient engagement, and revenue cycle management, into a single, integrated platform. The project is designed to reduce administrative burden and accelerate patient onboarding, while giving patients modern access to their own care journey. Artificial intelligence will be at the core of the platform. It is designed to power LailaCare's workflow end-to-end within home infusion pharmacy operations, identifying and routing referrals at intake, supporting eligibility and authorization, and scrubbing claims to help prevent denials in the revenue cycle, while keeping KabaFusion's trained staff in control of clinical and exception decisions. "KabaFusion has spent years building a reputation for high quality, patient-centered infusion care, and we are always looking for ways to strengthen that foundation," said Dr. Sohail Masood, Chairman and CEO of KabaFusion. "LailaCare is a natural next step for us. It will give our team the tools to work more efficiently and give our patients a more connected experience, while reinforcing the standard of care that has defined KabaFusion from the start." "CareCloud has spent 25 years building healthcare platforms at scale, and AI is now at the center of how we build," said Stephen Snyder, Chief Executive Officer of CareCloud. "LailaCare will pair KabaFusion's deep operational expertise in home infusion with CareCloud's technology and our AI Center of Excellence, exactly the kind of platform we are investing in, one designed to deliver measurable value to customers and to reflect the growing role of AI across our business." About CareCloud CareCloud brings disciplined innovation to the business of healthcare. Our suite of AI and technology-enabled solutions helps clients increase financial and operational performance, streamline clinical workflows and improve the patient experience. More than 40,000 providers count on CareCloud to help them improve patient care, while reducing administrative burdens and operating costs. Learn more about our products and services, including revenue cycle management (RCM), practice management (PM), electronic health records (EHR), business intelligence, patient experience management (PXM) and digital health, at carecloud.com . Follow CareCloud on LinkedIn , X and Facebook . For additional information, please visit our website at carecloud.com . To listen to video presentations by CareCloud’s management team, read recent press releases and view the latest investor presentation, please visit ir.carecloud.com . About KabaFusion KabaFusion is a national provider of chronic and acute infusion therapies. KabaFusion serves patients in 49 states through its nationwide network of home infusion pharmacies, ambulatory infusion suites, and home health agencies. KabaFusion was founded in 2010 by Chief Executive Officer Dr. Sohail Masood, a pioneer in patient-focused infusion therapies with more than 30 years of clinical experience. KabaFusion is dedicated to working proactively with patients, healthcare practitioners, and payors to provide comprehensive support before, during and after treatment. title: How ‘The Polygamist’ Is Breaking Records and Opening Doors in South Africa and Around the World
summary: Netflix's 22-episode supernovela has reached #1 in 21 countries and the Top 10 in 62, amassing 27.6 million views and counting.
body_text: At Netflix, we’ve seen over and over again how local stories can travel the globe. From South Korea ( Teach You a Lesson ), from France ( Lupin ), from Brazil ( Rulers of Fortune ) and now, from South Africa with The Polygamist . Based on the 2012 book of the same name by Zimbabwean author Sue Nyathi, The Polygamist debuted on Netflix June 12th and quickly became one of our biggest African hits ever. The 22-episode super novela has reached #1 in 21 countries and the Top 10 in 62, amassing 27.6M views and counting. Since opening at #2 on the Global Top 10 Non-English Shows list , the show has spent seven consecutive weeks on the list, the most ever for a Netflix title from South Africa. The series’ impact has extended beyond the screen, with book sales tripling following The Polygamist’s Netflix debut, over a decade after the book was first published. “It feels great and it is an affirmation of my work,” Nyathi said of the world’s reception to her story. “Of all my books, The Polygamist was dismissed as fluff. … To hear people call it a masterpiece and being able to draw so many life lessons from it is incredible.” The series, which centers on a social media darling whose cheating husband's conquests ignite a scandalous emotional meltdown, was filmed with Stained Glass Productions over nearly 100 days in South Africa. Roughly 150 cast and crew and over 70 extras and daily hires were employed on the production, in addition to more than 45 local vendors . "We were so specific and so particular in the story we're telling," said Gugu Zuma-Ncube, executive producer at Stained Glass Productions. "It's set against a backdrop of polygamy, which is very African — and the more authentic we were to that, the more universally appealing and relatable the themes became. Polygamy may not be the most common framework for a global audience, but the themes that the show covers - love, adultery, betrayal, struggling with feelings of self-worth, kids feeling they aren’t being met emotionally by their parents, coming‑of‑age - they definitely have universal appeal." From left to right: S'dumo Mtshali, director Rolie Nikiwe, Wonder Ndlovu, Murendeni Netshikandwana, first assistant director Thabani Gigaba, Gugu Gumede, Noluthando Shabalala, Rendani Netshikandwana and camera operator Isaura Afonso behind the scenes of ‘The Polygamist.’ (Courtesy of Netflix © 2026) Beyond The Polygamist , Nyathi says the Netflix series has helped “broaden” her readership. The same week The Polygamist hit #1 on the Exclusive Books’ Top 10 Bestsellers list in South Africa, her 2020 novel A Family Affair reached #6. The first run of her 2024 work, An Angel’s Demis e, also sold out following The Polygamist’ s Netflix debut, after only selling 2,500 copies in its first two years of release. The show’s popularity “has opened doors for me,” Nyathi said. “This series has given me the kind of visibility that writers from the deep south only dream of.” The Polygamist is one of several adaptations currently heating up our Global Top 10 lists, also including I Will Find You , Little House on the Prairie , Ransom Canyon , I’m Not Afraid and The Marked Woman . Netflix not only brings these books to the screen — we also turn these stories into culture-defining moments that spark new fandoms, expand worlds and bolster book sales and audiobook streams. Learn more about our latest adaptations here . The Polygamist is now streaming — only on Netflix. For more stories about the impact our films and series have on economies, industries and culture, check out The Netflix Effect .

title: Business valuation in Singapore: Methods, industry multiples and how to calculate
summary: Learn how business valuation works, compare key valuation methods and industry multiples, and calculate your business value in Singapore.
body_text: What is business valuation in Singapore and when do you actually need one Business valuation is the process of determining your company's economic worth at a specific point in time, using a defined method, for a defined purpose. The purpose of the valuation determines the method, and the method determines the number. There are four situations where a business valuation moves from useful to non-negotiable: Fundraising: Any institutional investor, be it angel, VC, or private equity, will form a view on your pre-money valuation before the first term sheet. If you have formed one first, you're set to have the upper hand during negotiations Mergers and acquisitions: Whether you're acquiring or being acquired, the valuation is the foundation of every deal term that follows: price, earnout structure, working capital adjustment, representations and warranties ESOP issuance: In Singapore, issuing equity to employees requires a defensible valuation of the underlying shares. A well-documented valuation prevents both regulatory exposure and employee relations risk Shareholder exits and disputes: An independent valuation is the most reliable mechanism for resolving shareholder disagreements about price and for structuring clean exits without litigation risk There is a fifth trigger most CFOs underuse . Internal strategic benchmarking. Using a valuation as a periodic health check against competitors, your own prior round, or sector multiples is what separates finance functions that inform strategy from those that report history. For Singapore-registered businesses , the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) and the Institute of Valuers and Appraisers Singapore (IVAS) provide the professional framework. IRAS guidelines for asset transfers and certain corporate restructuring events mean valuation isn't always discretionary. Best practice: If your business is 18 months from a potential exit or next raise, the time to establish a baseline valuation is now, not when the counterparty asks for one. Valuations prepared under transaction pressure are rarely as defensible as those built without it. Business valuation methods and which one applies to your company There is no universally correct method. The right approach depends on your company's stage, the predictability of your revenue, and what the valuation will be used for. Most professional valuers use more than one method and triangulate to a range. In fact, a single-method valuation is a red flag in any investor or acquirer diligence process. Income approach: Discounted cash flow (DCF) The DCF method values your business by estimating its future free cash flows and discounting them back to their present value using a risk-adjusted rate (the Weighted Average Cost of Capital, or WACC). Best for: Growth-stage companies with two to three years of predictable revenue history and a credible forward forecast. This is the most commonly used method in fundraising because it forces both parties to agree on growth assumptions, not just historical earnings. How it works: Project annual free cash flows over a five to ten-year period. Apply a terminal value to capture value beyond the forecast window. Discount the total to present value using your WACC (which typically ranges between 15% and 25% for Singapore-based SMEs), depending on sector risk and capital structure. Example: A B2B SaaS company generating SGD $2 million in annual recurring revenue, growing at 30% year-on-year with 70% gross margins and a 20% WACC, might produce a DCF valuation in the range of SGD $8 million to SGD $12 million, depending entirely on the terminal growth rate assumption. Move that assumption from 3% to 5% and the valuation shifts by 25%. Market approach: Comparable companies and transaction multiples The market approach values your business by comparing it to similar companies that have been sold or funded recently, applying a multiple to your earnings or revenue. Best for: Businesses in sectors with active M&A activity or where comparable funded companies exist — eCommerce, professional services, technology. This is the most commonly used method for mainstream SME transactions in Singapore. How it works: Identify comparable companies or recent transactions. Apply the relevant multiple (EV/Revenue, EV/EBITDA, or SDE multiple) to your own financial metric. Adjust for company-specific risk factors like customer concentration, revenue quality, and founder dependency. What Singapore-based businesses should consider: In Singapore, 2×–5× EBITDA is the standard range for most mainstream SME transactions, meaningfully lower than Malaysia (3×–6×) or Thailand (7×–10×). The multiple you receive sits within that range based on how well your business performs against the risk factors investors and acquirers apply. Business valuation multiples by industry in Singapore and Southeast Asia (2025): [Table:1] All multiples reflect global and regional private market transaction data. Singapore SME transactions in mainstream sectors (FMCG, F&B, professional services) typically trade at 2×–5× EBITDA, at the lower end of comparable international ranges, reflecting market size, buyer pool depth, and liquidity factors specific to the Singapore M&A market. Asset-based approach: Net asset value The asset-based approach values your business by calculating the net value of its assets, that is, total assets minus total liabilities. It comes in two variants: going concern (adjusted book value) and liquidation value. Best for: Asset-heavy businesses, property holding companies, or businesses in financial distress. It is also relevant for multi-entity structures in Singapore where a property-holding entity and an operating entity are linked; each needs to be valued on appropriate terms. What it misses: For eCommerce, SaaS, and professional services businesses, the primary audience for this guide. Asset-based valuation almost always understates economic value. It captures what you own, not what you generate or what the market will pay for your earnings stream. Startup valuation: When there are no earnings to model For pre-revenue or early-revenue companies, traditional financial methods produce numbers that are either unreliable or meaningless. Startup valuation methods substitute financial history with team quality, market size, traction signals, and investor risk tolerance. Key methods: Berkus method: Assigns a value (typically up to SGD $2.5 million) to five non-financial factors: viable idea, prototype, quality management team, strategic relationships, and product rollout or revenue. Simple and transparent, it is useful for very early-stage conversations Scorecard method: Benchmarks the startup against regional comparable funded companies, then adjusts the average pre-money valuation based on weighted factors including team strength, market opportunity, competitive positioning, and technology moat Venture Capital method: Works backwards from the investor's required return. If the investor needs 10× return and expects to exit at SGD $50 million in five years, the pre-money valuation is implied by the ownership percentage required to deliver that return Entry cost method: Values the startup by estimating what it would cost to rebuild the business from scratch — technology, IP, hiring, and customer acquisition included. Useful for hardware and deep tech startups, but limited as a standalone method because it captures current asset value, not future earnings potential Future valuation multiple method: Projects revenue or EBITDA at a defined future point, applies a sector-appropriate multiple to arrive at a future enterprise value, then discounts back to today. Most applicable at Series A or traction stage, when forward projections are credible enough to hold up to investor scrutiny Risk factor summation method: Starts with the average pre-money valuation of comparable funded startups in the same region and sector, then adjusts that baseline up or down based on 12 standard risk factors (including management risk, market competition risk, technology risk, legislative risk, and capital raising risk) Singapore context: Enterprise Singapore grants and SGInnovate co-investment schemes are material inputs to startup valuation. Non-dilutive capital reduces the risk premium that investors apply. A company with SGD $500,000 in government grants already deployed has de-risked its early milestones in a way that moves a pre-money negotiation. Watch out for: DCF is highly sensitive to discount rate and terminal value inputs. A 1% change in either can move the total valuation by 20–30%. Any investor will run their own model, which is why your assumptions need to be documented and coherent, not optimistic. How to calculate business valuation: A step-by-step guide Before engaging a valuation advisor, a CFO can complete an internal baseline in six steps: Step 1 — Define the purpose Fundraising , M&A, ESOP, or internal benchmark. The purpose determines the method, which determines the inputs you need to prepare. Step 2 — Normalise your finances. Calculate adjusted EBITDA by removing owner-specific expenses that will not continue post-transaction, one-off items (litigation costs, restructuring), and non-cash charges. This is your true earnings baseline. Step 3 — Choose your method Apply DCF if you have a credible multi-year forecast. Apply market multiples if comparable transactions exist in your sector. Use both where possible and triangulate. Step 4 — Build a range, not a single number A valuation presented as a single figure invites a counterparty to attack the assumptions. A range, supported by methodology, gives you room to negotiate without appearing defensive. Step 5 — Stress-test against comparables Run your number against publicly available transaction data for your sector. If you are significantly above or below the range, understand why and be able to articulate that difference confidently. Step 6 — Document every assumption The model is not the valuation. The assumptions behind the model are what get interrogated in a diligence process. Revenue growth rate, churn, margin expansion, and discount rate need a source and a rationale. Business valuation in mergers and acquisitions: What changes M&A valuation is not the same exercise as fundraising valuation. The lens shifts from growth potential to synergy value, integration risk, and what the business is worth to a specific buyer, not to the market in general. For CFOs at multi-entity companies, several additional factors come into play: Consolidation and intercompany adjustments: An acquirer will look at group-level EBITDA after eliminating intercompany transactions. If your Singapore entity bills a regional subsidiary at an above-market rate, that revenue disappears in consolidation, and so does the multiple applied to it Transfer pricing: Cross-border intercompany pricing must be documented and defensible under IRAS guidelines. In an M&A context, an acquirer's tax advisor will review transfer pricing as part of diligence. Misaligned pricing creates both valuation risk and post-close tax exposure Net working capital : Most M&A transactions include a net working capital adjustment at close. A business with volatile debtor days or poorly managed inventory will have a larger working capital peg, which reduces the cash consideration the seller ultimately receives Earnout structures: Buyers use earnout provisions to bridge valuation gaps. Understanding how earnouts interact with your post-close operating model (and whether you retain enough control to hit the targets) is as important as the headline valuation number Choosing between business valuation advisors: For straightforward SME transactions in Singapore, an IVAS-accredited business valuation firm (SGD $3,000–$10,000) provides the methodology and report. For complex cross-border or multi-entity deals, an investment bank or Big 4 M&A advisory practice provides the full sell-side or buy-side mandate at a substantially higher cost. Know which engagement you are in before you sign an advisory mandate What actually moves your valuation and what your finance workflow controls Four levers sit directly within the finance function's control: Revenue quality: Recurring versus transactional revenue, customer concentration, and churn rate are the three variables that move your multiple most significantly. A business with 80% recurring revenue and net revenue retention above 100% commands a meaningfully higher multiple than one at identical EBITDA with lumpy, project-based income. This is a structuring decision, not an accounting one and it should be made years before a transaction. Financial visibility: Investors and acquirers apply a risk discount when they cannot trust the numbers. Financials that are reconciled monthly, with clear cost allocation across entities and transparent intercompany flows, reduce the information asymmetry that drives discounts. Clean, current data is a negotiating asset. Working capital efficiency: Buyers model working capital at close. A business with predictable cash conversion cycles, low days sales outstanding, and disciplined payables management presents lower operational risk and the market prices that accordingly. Operational independence: Founder or key-person dependency is one of the largest single valuation discounts applied in SME and mid-market deals. Finance teams that can demonstrate process-driven operations, where outputs are not dependent on any individual's institutional knowledge, reduce the risk premium the acquirer applies. For CFOs building towards an exit or next raise, the finance function's infrastructure is directly linked to the valuation outcome. When financial data is always current, assumptions are always auditable, and processes are built to run without individual intervention, the risk discount applied to your business narrows. That gap between a defended valuation and a discounted one, often lives inside the finance function itself, not in the market. Common business valuation mistakes that reduce credibility Common mistakes include: Using revenue instead of quality revenue Applying industry multiples without matching company profile Ignoring debt, cash, and working capital Overstating recurring revenue Ignoring customer concentration Treating forecast as fact Using one method only Not separating entity-level financial performance Ignoring FX and cross-border tax exposure Not documenting assumptions A valuation is only as credible as the evidence behind it. How Aspire supports valuation-ready finance operations For CFOs and finance leaders preparing for valuation, the question is not only, “What multiple should we use?” It is, “Can our finance systems prove the quality of our revenue, cash flow, spend controls, and entity-level performance?” Valuation depends on real-time financial visibility. Multi-entity companies need cleaner spend governance, cash visibility, payment workflows, accounts payable discipline, and accounting data. AspireOS acts as the intelligence layer for global business by helping companies execute financial policy. Its spend management solution helps you govern spend through autonomous guardrails, while Aspire Accounting supports a more continuous close and cleaner financial data. Together, these workflows help finance teams scale transaction volume and headcount without scaling finance admin at the same pace. The better your finance operations, the more defensible your valuation story becomes. FAQs What is business valuation and why does it matter? Business valuation is the process of determining your company's economic worth at a specific point in time using a defined methodology. It matters because it determines your negotiating position in fundraising, M&A, ESOP issuance, and shareholder exits, and because the method used can produce materially different numbers from the same financial data. What are the main business valuation methods? Three approaches cover the vast majority of valuations: the income approach (DCF), the market approach (comparable company multiples and precedent transactions), and the asset-based approach (net asset value). Most professional valuers apply more than one and triangulate to a range. How do I value a startup with no revenue in Singapore? Pre-revenue startups are typically valued using the Berkus Method, Scorecard Method, or Venture Capital Method, each of which substitutes financial history with team quality, market size, and traction signals. Enterprise Singapore and SGInnovate co-investment schemes can positively influence pre-money positioning by reducing perceived risk. What are typical business valuation multiples by industry in Singapore? For mainstream Singapore SMEs, 2×–5× EBITDA is the standard range. Sector-specific multiples vary significantly: SaaS businesses command 4.8×–7.3× ARR; eCommerce trades at 2.8×–5.0× profit; professional services typically sit at 2.0×–3.5× EBITDA. Company-specific factors like revenue quality, concentration, and founder dependency move the final number within those ranges. When do I need a business valuation in Singapore? Fundraising, M&A (buy or sell side), ESOP issuance, and shareholder exits or disputes all require a defensible valuation. IRAS guidelines also make professional valuation necessary for certain asset transfers and corporate restructuring events. Proactive internal benchmarking is a practice the most well-prepared finance functions maintain annually. What is the difference between valuation for fundraising versus M&A? Fundraising valuation focuses on growth potential and future earnings; the investor is buying into what the business can become. M&A valuation focuses on what the business is worth to a specific acquirer, accounting for synergies, integration risk, and working capital. The buyer is pricing what they can extract. The same business can produce meaningfully different numbers under each lens. How much does a business valuation cost in Singapore? Professional SME valuations typically range from SGD $3,000 to SGD $10,000, depending on complexity and the scope of the engagement. Multi-entity or cross-border valuations for M&A purposes cost more, particularly when conducted by Big 4 or investment banking advisors who charge a retainer plus a success fee.

Bank of Hawai‘i Announces New Executive Vice President Nathan Lee
summary: Bank of Hawai‘i Announces New Executive Vice President Nathan Lee
body_text: Nathan Lee recently joined Bank of Hawai‘i as executive vice president and executive director of strategic initiatives, where he will provide enterprise-wide leadership to shape, direct and oversee execution of the bank’s highest-priority strategic initiatives. He will oversee complex, cross-enterprise transformation efforts, shape governance structures and operating models, and provide executive-level insight on execution health, systemic risk, and organizational readiness. Lee will also partner with the bank’s team on its Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) program, helping advance and strengthen compliance efforts and the broader control framework. Lee brings more than 20 years of experience in public and private financial statement audits, risk assessment, internal controls, governance, and advisory services. Prior to joining the bank, he worked at Ernst & Young LLP across the firm’s Irvine, California, and Honolulu offices, where he managed a portfolio of clients in the financial services industry, including commercial banking, consumer lending, fintech, and captive insurance. He also led recruiting for the Honolulu office assurance practice and established the EY Excellence Fund to provide scholarships for University of Hawai‘i students. A Certified Public Accountant licensed in Hawai‘i and California, Lee is a member of the American Institute of CPAs and the Hawaii Society of CPAs. He holds a Master of Science in Accountancy from the University of Notre Dame and a Bachelor of Science in Management from Brigham Young University in Provo, Utah. Lee most recently served for eight years on the Junior Achievement of Hawai‘i Board of Directors and its Audit Committee and actively holds a leadership role within his church.

title: RingCentral pricing: Plans, hidden fees & what you actually pay
summary: Get a full breakdown of RingCentral pricing in this article. Find out which features are available in its plans compared to its add-ons.
body_text: RingCentral has been a major business phone provider since the 1990s. But its pricing isn’t as straightforward as it seems. With six different offers, 14+ add-ons, and hidden fees, you might end up paying more than you expected. Here’s what you need to know. RingCentral’s RingEX business phone plans cost $20 to $35 per user per month on an annual contract. If you opt for monthly billing, the cost ranges from $30 to $45 per user per month. That published price is only the starting point. Add-ons, per-user SMS and toll-free overage charges, and directory-assistance fees are billed on top. The amount you actually pay is often higher than the plan’s sticker price. In this article, we’ll cover RingCentral’s pricing and plans in detail. We’ll also show you why RingCentral’s platform isn’t as affordable as you think. By the end of this article, you’ll understand why RingCentral isn’t worth the price for small businesses. RingCentral business phone plans and pricing RingEX is RingCentral’s business phone for every workday communication. It provides phone calls, texts, video meetings, and other basic communication features. There are four separate RingEX plans to choose from, each with different limits on messages, minutes, and features. These limits can affect how your team communicates with customers and each other as call and text volume grows. Here are the main differences side-by-side: Feature Core Advanced Ultra Customer Engagement Bundle Price per user per month $20 annually/$30 monthly $25 annually/$35 monthly $35 annually/$45 monthly Pricing isn’t public Best for Startups with low or unpredictable text and call volumes Businesses with automation and CRM integration needs Businesses with high call volumes and advanced reporting needs Large teams managing high inbound call volume that need advanced call queuing Text messaging 25 SMS/MMS per user per month 100 SMS/MMS per user per month 200 SMS/MMS per user per month 200 SMS/MMS per user per month Toll-free minutes 100 pooled 1,000 pooled 10,000 pooled 10,000 pooled Storage Limited Limited “Unlimited” excludes video recordings “Unlimited” excludes video recordings Call recording On-demand Automatic/on-demand Automatic/on-demand Automatic/on-demand AI-powered call summaries ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ AI-assisted message writing X ✓ ✓ ✓ Analytics Basic reports Custom analytics Custom analytics, device alerts Custom analytics, device alerts, and live reports CRM integrations X ✓ ✓ ✓ RingEX Core plan Pricing : $20 per user per month paid annually or $30 per user per month paid monthly Best for : Solo operators or very small teams that primarily make calls and rarely text The Core plan includes basic VoIP features and unlimited calls in the US and Canada. Here’s what you can expect to get: Calling: Unlimited calls in the US and Canada Texting: 25 SMS and MMS messages per user per month Toll-free minutes: 100 pooled Shared numbers: Calls only Call recording storage: Limited; for example, recordings are automatically deleted after 90 days Call routing: Multi-level auto-attendants Integrations: Microsoft Teams, Office 365, and Slack Video meetings: Up to 100 participants Call recording: On-demand RingEX Advanced plan Pricing: $25 per user per month paid annually or $35 per user per month paid monthly Best for: Teams that want a few more communication tools but don’t need unlimited storage or flexibility The Advanced plan unlocks higher limits for texts and toll-free minutes. You’ll get access to the following features: Texting: 100 SMS and MMS messages per user per month Toll-free minutes : 1,000 pooled Call recording: On-demand and automatic call recording is available Integrations: CRM integrations, such as Salesforce and Zendesk Call queues: Advanced, which means you can route calls to specific reps based on criteria, like max callers in a queue Call monitoring: Whisper, barge, and monitor But the Advanced plan doesn’t offer unlimited storage for files, messaging, and recordings. Plus, many of its advanced features require add-ons to maximize their value. For example, there’s no way to join third-party video meetings in a conference room without purchasing the Rooms add-on. Keep in mind, it costs $39 per room per month. RingEX Ultra plan Pricing : $35 per user per month paid annually or $45 per user per month paid monthly Best for : Call centers that want more toll-free minutes, even if texting is still capped. RingCentral’s Ultra plan unlocks features best suited to larger organizations. You’ll get access to the following tools: Texting: 200 SMS and MMS messages per user per month Toll-free minutes: 10,000 pooled Storage : Unlimited, doesn’t include video recordings, and retention periods still apply Webinars: Host large meetings with up to 500 attendees Analytics: Device analytics and alerts You should know the ‘unlimited’ storage doesn’t include video meetings. Plus, all your files are subject to time-based deletion policies. For example, your call recordings will be deleted after 90 days. There are also limits on RingCentral SMS and toll-free minutes. This could get frustrating as your business grows. RingEX Customer Engagement Bundle Pricing : Not publicly listed Best for : Larger teams that handle a lot of calls and need advanced call queues. The Customer Engagement Bundle builds on the RingEX Ultra plan while also giving you access to two of its add-ons: Business SMS Booster and Call Queues Booster. Here are the features you can expect to get with each: Business SMS Booster : Shared SMS inbox, company reply templates, SMS compliance management Call Queues Booster : Call back from queue, wait time, and place alerts, and live reports Keep in mind that even with the most expensive plan, you still won’t get access to add-ons like push-to-talk or unlimited toll-free minutes. Which RingCentral RingEx plan should you choose? With four different options, it can be tough to choose a RingEx plan that works for your team. Here’s a quick checklist you can use to find the right RingEx plan for your business: Texting volume. How many texts do you send monthly? A rough estimate can help you choose the most appropriate plan. If you send fewer messages per month, you should go with the Core plan. If your text volume is growing quickly, opt for the Advanced or Ultra plans. Unlimited storage for messages, files, and recordings. If storage is your biggest priority, you should go with the Ultra plan. However, you should know that even with this plan, your call recordings are automatically deleted after 90 days. CRM integrations. Do you need to connect your RingEX account to your CRM? If CRM integrations are a must-have, you’ll have to go with the Advanced or Ultra plans. CRM connections aren’t available in the Core plan. Customer support call volume. Similar to texting volume, toll-free call volume scales with each tier in RingCentral. You get access to 100 minutes in the Core plan, 1,000 minutes in the Advanced plan, and 10,000 minutes in the Ultra plan. Estimate how many customer support calls you currently receive and choose a plan that can accommodate your monthly volume. Otherwise, you might end up paying more for toll-free overages. RingCentral plans add-ons RingCentral offers 14 separate add-ons for RingEX plans. They include: Add-on option Cost Additional vanity phone numbers $4.99 set-up fee, plus a $30 one-time fee Additional international numbers Starts at $5.99 per user per month Additional toll-free or local numbers $4.99 per user per month Additional international toll-free numbers $14.99 per user per month plus a $25 one-time fee High Volume SMS Starts at $0.01 per message sent and received RingCentral Rooms license Starts at $39 per room per month RingCentral Webinar™ $30 per organizer per month AI Conversation Expert $60 per user per month Push-to-Talk license $5 per user per month RingCentral Events Starts at $99 per organizer per year RingCX AI Contact Center $65 per user Business SMS Booster $25 per user per month Call Queues Booster $35 per user per month AI Receptionist $39 per month RingCentral AI Receptionist add-on Pricing: $39 per account per month with 100 minutes included RingCentral’s AI receptionist can answer calls 24/7, book appointments, handle FAQs, and send automated texts. Plus, you can customize the AI voice agent’s tone and personality. But there are a few catches: You only get 100 calling minutes per month included, and additional minutes cost $0.50 per minute. AI call summaries aren’t included. Only available ‌in the US, Canada, Australia, the UK, and Europe. Some features vary depending on the country you’re in. You can use the AI Receptionist on its own with another phone system. You can also combine it with a RingEX account, which is available at a bundle discount for teams. In this bundle, AI Receptionist starts at $39 per month, compared to its standalone pricing of $49 per month. RingCentral Contact Center pricing If you need a more advanced business phone system , you may want a RingCentral Contact Center plan: RingCX Standard plan Pricing : $65 per user per month paid annually or $75 per user per month paid monthly The Standard plan is made for large contact center teams that need to route inbound calls and messages across multiple reps and channels. You’ll get access to the following features: Channels : Voice and 20+ digital channels, such as social media and email Routing : Automatic call distribution , IVR, and skills-based routing Dialer : Preview dialer that lets reps view lead info before they call, Progressive dialer that pauses for a certain amount of time in between making calls, and the Predictive dialer that automatically dials leads and only connects your reps to answered calls Queue callback : Callers have the option to request a callback Surveys : Create and manage surveys RingCX Professional plan Pricing : $95 per user per month paid annually or $110 per user per month paid monthly RingCentral’s CX Professional plan builds on the Standard plan with tools that support call center reps during live calls. You can expect to get access to the following features: Coaching tools : Real-time guidance given to reps during live calls Quality management : Post-call analysis with transcripts, summaries, and call scores to give you insights into how your reps perform RingCX Elite plan Pricing : $145 per user per month paid annually or $165 per user per month paid monthly The Elite plan adds more tools for supervisors who need help managing their teams without adding overhead. Here are the features it includes: Interaction analytics : Automatically extract CSAT insights from customer interactions Supervisor tools : Real-time alerts flag pressing calls to supervisors so they can step in and help Workforce management : AI forecasts that help you determine the number of staff you’ll need to work certain shifts RingCX Enterprise plan Pricing : Not publicly listed The Enterprise plan is ideal for teams that need to build knowledge bases that reps can access during live calls. Here are the features you can expect to get: Advanced call routing : Connect customers to the best rep with the skills and knowledge to help them Knowledge management : Knowledge base with saved responses reps can access while on calls RingCentral Video pricing If all you need are video conferencing tools to improve the customer experience, RingCentral offers the following plans: Free Meetings plan Meetings is a free plan that unlocks 50-minute video meetings for up to 200 participants. Keep in mind you have limited storage unless you purchase RingEx Ultra or higher. Here are the key features you’ll get access to: Unlimited video meetings for up to 200 participants Join from any device, room, or browser One click to turn phone calls into video meetings AI-powered meeting notes, summaries, and live transcriptions Town Halls webinar Pricing : $30 per organizer per month paid annually or $54 per user per month paid monthly RingCentral allows you to host webinars with up to 10,000 attendees with the Town Halls add-on. However, each organizer’s license only includes 500 attendees. This is available on any RingCentral video plan, and its features include: AI writing generator to help you create descriptions for your webinars Registration and branding tools that let you create banner images to use for registration pages Post-event reporting Q&A translation in over 15 languages Polling and Q&A tools Rooms Pricing : $39 per room per month paid annually or $49 per room per month paid monthly RingCentral’s Rooms add-on allows you to set up a conference room solution for your existing video plan. Just keep in mind it’s only compatible with enterprise-grade hardware, such as HP Poly and Yealink, if you’re using legacy desk phone hardware. Here are the features you can expect to get if you sign up for this add-on: One-touch join for Zoom, Teams, Google, Webex, and RingCentral meetings Schedule meetings Join third-party meetings Mobile-to-room conference calls Voice-activated control Background noise reduction Deliver presentations Webinars & Events Pricing : $99 per organizer per month paid annually or $119 per organizer per month paid monthly RingCentral Events lets you host virtual events and webinars with no cap on registrations or attendees. You’ll get access to the following features: Unlimited registrations and attendees Detailed event reporting, like engagement scores and org-level analytics AI tools like webinar writing and Q&A categorization Identify and generate clips of your webinar after it has ended RingCentral Events pricing Thinking about holding events for your business? RingCentral’s Events plans allow you to hold virtual, onsite, or hybrid events with unlimited attendees per event. It offers the following plans: Events Pro plan Pricing : $99 per organizer per month paid annually or $119 per organizer per month paid monthly The Events Pro plan is best for teams that run virtual events frequently and need basic tools to get up and running. Here are the features you can expect to get: Unlimited webinars and virtual events AI-powered webinars that include AI features like AI Writer that creates webinar descriptions Unlimited registrations for your events Virtual venue that lets you create up to five stages to host keynotes, presentations, and more Paid and free ticketing options Event analytics and reporting Studio-quality production tools that allow you to upload content like music and video before your event starts Standard support Events Pro+ plan Pricing : $199 per organizer per month paid annually or $239 per organizer per month paid monthly The Events Pro+ plan is great for hybrid events and deeper engagement. It includes everything in Pro, plus the following features: 40+ engagement app integrations like Kahoot, Miro, and Slido Over five MarTech integrations, like Marketo, HubSpot, Salesforce, Mailchimp, and Active Campaign On-site and hybrid event support Single sign-on, or SSO Dedicated customer success manager Events Enterprise plan Pricing : $299 per organizer per month paid annually or $359 per organizer per month paid monthly The Events Enterprise plan is built for large-scale, complex events. It includes everything in Pro+, plus you can also expect to get features such as: Lead retrieval tools that let you gather leads by scanning an attendee’s QR code on their badge to follow up with them later API access to integrate RingCentral Events and other tools Custom domains for your events Content hubs for repurposing event assets RingCentral Conversation Intelligence pricing Pricing : $60 per user per month Conversation Intelligence unlocks AI-driven coaching, performance analysis, and personalized reporting tools. Here’s a closer look at the features you’ll get: Multi-level reporting and insights Advanced search, sort, and interaction filtering Deal and call scoring Automated summaries and highlights Coaching and performance analysis CRM integrations Hidden fees to know about RingCentral pricing Here are some additional fees to consider before signing on the dotted line for RingCentral: Texting limits . No plan offers unlimited texts. The Core plan is limited to 25 texts per user per month, the Advanced plan offers 100 texts, and the Ultra plan comes with only 200 texts. After that, you’ll need to pay $0.0085 per message. Toll-free calling limits . As with texting, no RingCentral plan includes unlimited toll-free minutes. The Core plan gives you 100 minutes pooled across the entire account , followed by the Advanced plan at 1,000 minutes and the Ultra plan at 10,000 minutes. Toll-free SMS charges . You can send up to 50 messages per minute, and you’ll be charged $0.0085 per message sent or received by your toll-free number. Advanced business analytics. You only have access to basic analytics unless you upgrade to the Advanced plan. It costs $25 per user per month. Directory assistance, or 411. If you need access to National Local Directory Assistance, be prepared to pay $1 per call. Number setup fee. Each toll-free vanity number requires a one-time setup fee of $30. International calling and SMS. RingCentral lists its international call rates online. But its international SMS rates are only available in the Admin portal. This means there’s no way to know how much you’ll pay for international texts until you sign up for a plan to take the free trial. Regular billing issues. Past RingCentral users frequently report billing issues with the company. That includes billing for service after cancellation and overcharging customers. We’re not kidding — billing issues are a consistent problem with RingCentral. Take these reviews from Quo users who switched from RingCentral: “ RingCentral’s service and billing are a nightmare. Constant errors, unclear charges, and their support team is useless at best. We’ve spent countless hours trying to fix basic billing issues, and it feels like they couldn’t care less. ” — RingCentral user on G2 “ This company is only interested in ripping you off. They were charging me 950 a month for using 8 lines and would not let me out of the contract as I had sold off a portion of my business and reduced the size of my company! Even though I had been their client for over 10 years – there is no flexibility. ” — RingCentral user on G2 “ The contract has an auto-renewal feature for an additional two years, so after two years, I was opted in by contract with no notification and stuck. Then, when the contract was over, I canceled half of my lines and was assured this was done. They continue to charge me for these lines and refuse to respond to my requests for review. ” — RingCentral user on G2 What’s missing from RingCentral plans Here are a few more reasons to consider RingCentral alternatives : Shared numbers for texting. You can use RingCentral to set up shared phone numbers for calling, allowing your team to split responsibility for calls. But there’s no way to share responsibility for incoming texts unless you pay for an add-on. You also won’t find many texting automation tools with RingCentral — at least not out of the box. You may need to hire a developer to use RingCentral Automator or upgrade your plan to access third-party integrations. “The ability to share SMS inboxes with other members of my team is absolutely critical. I don’t know how any small business that communicates by SMS with their customers can survive without this functionality. It is the key feature that got us to switch from RingCentral.” — Quo user on G2 Transparent US texting registration process. If your business plans to send texts through RingCentral, be prepared for a lengthy registration process. RingCentral requires businesses to register with The Campaign Registry, or TCR , to comply with carrier regulations. While the $19 one-time TCR fee is standard, the approval timeline is long. According to RingCentral’s TCR registration page, the process takes 20–30 business days. But many users report waiting months to get approved. In contrast, Quo, formerly OpenPhone, has received some approvals in as little as 5–7 business days. Unified team inbox. Every call, text, and voicemail in RingCentral lives in separate inboxes. There’s no way to see all these touchpoints in one place, which can increase the time it takes to get up to speed on a conversation. Storage for recordings, files, and more. By far, the biggest drawback of how RingCentral works is its lack of unlimited storage. Automatic and on-demand call recordings expire after 90 days, faxes expire after 30 days, and call logs expire after 12 months. You can only store 5,000 SMS/MMS messages per user per account. And after 200 unheard voicemails, new messages begin saving over old files. Simple user interface. RingCentral’s interface is clunky and outdated. This makes it frustrating and time-consuming to customize it to your liking. Most business platforms, including Quo, make it simple and intuitive to navigate your VoIP phone number. Setting up snippets takes a few minutes or less, and you don’t need to learn how to code. Full access free trial. Although RingCentral does offer a free trial, its limitations make it almost unusable. You’re limited to five users and two desktop phones. If you have a team larger than five people, you can’t try it out for yourself before you sign up. Is RingCentral pricing cost-effective for small businesses? If you’re just getting started or growing fast, your business phone should be able to scale with you. That includes the features it offers and how it prices them. RingCentral’s pricing can be prohibitive for small businesses. With limits on texting, add-ons for essential features like shared SMS, and billing issues with contract lock-in, your bills can run up quickly. Text limits SMS messaging has changed how businesses and customers communicate, and the numbers back it up. A 2025 study found that 86% of customers will opt in to receiving texts from a business, compared to just 66% in 2021. Unfortunately, RingCentral limits how many texts you can send in each plan. Once you hit your monthly limit, you have to pay for each message you send to your customers. This pricing model is hard to estimate, making it difficult for small teams to budget their phone costs each month. Add-ons for essential features RingCentral offers SMS and MMS messaging in each of its plans. However, if you want to tackle customer communications in a shared inbox, you have to purchase its Business SMS Booster add-on for an additional $25 per month. Similarly, you need to purchase this booster if you want access to text templates. Other business phone platforms like Quo include these features in its plans without charging you for add-ons. Limited texting access after sign up Another reason RingCentral isn’t great for small businesses is you can’t access texting immediately. Business texting registration is required to text US phone numbers. However, RingCentral’s registration process can take months, according to customers. It means that you can’t take advantage of business texting as quickly as you may want. Quo: A better alternative to RingCentral plans If you have deep pockets or plenty of patience, you might be able to make RingCentral work for you. However, if you hate the idea of limitations and don’t have the budget for constant add-ons, RingCentral will be more of a liability. This isn’t just a RingCentral problem — dozens of VoIP service providers don’t make the cut for small business owners. That’s why so many of them turn to a more efficient business phone service — including Quo, the #1 small business phone service on G2. Take a closer look at Quo vs RingCentral side-by-side: Features Quo RingCentral Starting price per month $15 per user per month $20 per user per month Unlimited calling ✓ ✓ Unlimited SMS, MMS to US & Canada ✓ X Toll-free numbers Unlimited Minutes are limited Additional phone numbers $5 per number $4.99–$14.99 per number Call recording ✓ ✓ Shared phone numbers ✓ Calling only without an upgrade Auto-replies ✓ Requires Automator Text message templates ✓ Requires Business SMS Booster add-on or Customer Engagement Bundle plan AI Receptionist ✅, first 10 calls free $39 per month Slack integration ✓ ✓ Gmail integration ✓ ✓ Make integration ✓ X Web-based, iOS, and Android apps ✓ ✓ Free trial 7-day free trial 14-day free trial Don’t just take our word for it. Hear from users who’ve switched from RingCentral to Quo: “I switched from RingCentral to Quo for way better pricing, way better customer service, and a phone system that is always improving its functionality to better serve its customers.” – Bob Richey, Owner, Party Magic Entertainment Should you still use RingCentral? For many small and growing teams, RingCentral can feel limiting and expensive as their businesses scale. RingCentral works best for: Solopreneurs who mainly make calls and rarely text Large call centers with fixed, high-volume calling volume Teams with dedicated IT support to manage setup and maintenance RingCentral is less ideal for: Teams that need access to unlimited texts in the US and Canada Businesses that want clear, predictable pricing as they scale Growing teams that want to scale without losing a personal touch Pros and cons of RingCentral pricing plans Here are some of the pros and cons of RingCentral : Pros Web, desktop, and mobile apps for iOS and Android Offers VoIP inbound and outbound calls, business texts, call transfers, and video conferencing Team messaging and file-sharing tools are built into every plan Cons Limited business SMS, 25 texts per user per month on the base plan Limited toll-free minutes, 10,000 pooled minutes per month max Limited storage; even ‘unlimited’ comes with time and account-based retention limits Final verdict: Choose Quo for better pricing and team collaboration RingCentral is a decent example of what a cloud-based VoIP phone could be. But it’s not a great example of a transparent, accessible, and scalable platform. The good news is that Quo picks up where RingCentral leaves off. Curious to see how Quo does things differently? Try Quo today with our seven-day free trial . FAQs What are the best RingCentral alternatives? RingCentral’s competitors include business phone platforms like Quo, Dialpad, Vonage, and Google Voice. Here’s a quick overview: – RingCentral vs Quo. Quo has a better user interface, so your team can start helping right away without significant training. Plus, Quo doesn’t have SMS/MMS or outbound toll-free minute limits. – RingCentral vs Dialpad . Dialpad offers video conferencing and unlimited calling and texting in the United States and Canada, though Dialpad texting has some limitations. – RingCentral vs Vonage . Vonage has more API options for customization and a better library of integrations. – RingCentral vs Google Voice . Google Voice starts at $10 per user per month, but far fewer business features, no advanced call routing, and limited support. It often can’t scale with a growing business. See our full Google Voice vs RingCentral comparison. How much does RingCentral cost per month? RingCentral’s monthly cost depends on your plan and billing cycle. On an annual contract, plans range from $20 to $35 per user per month. Month-to-month billing is 30–50% more expensive: $30, $35, or $45 per user per month, respectively. Add-on fees, toll-free overage costs, and SMS overage charges are extra. How much does RingCX cost? RingCX’s pricing starts at $65 per agent per month. This includes call recording, IVR , a predictive dialer, and skills-based routing. What are some tips to save money on RingCentral? Here are some practical tips to save money on RingCentral: – Pay annually to save up to 30% compared to monthly pricing. – Only add essential users to avoid unnecessary seat costs. – Start with a lower-tier plan and upgrade only if needed. – Watch for overages on texts and toll-free minutes to avoid extra fees. – Skip unused add-ons like webinars or events. – Negotiate with sales for discounts, especially for larger teams. – Try a provider like Quo for more value at a lower cost. Is RingCentral cheaper than Zoom? Zoom Phone’s pricing starts at $10 per user per month, while RingCentral’s base plan costs $20 per user per month. On the surface, Zoom Phone looks like the cheaper option if you’re only comparing entry-level prices. But its $10 base plan is metered, which means you’ll pay extra for every outbound minute. Once you factor in usage, costs can add up quickly. Is RingCentral HIPAA compliant? Yes, RingCentral is a HIPAA-compliant VoIP provider. But you’ll need to request a Business Associate Agreement, also known as BAA, if you want to access your clients’ Protected Health Information, PHI. What are users saying about RingCentral’s pricing? Users say RingCentral looks affordable upfront, but ends up being expensive. One user said they were locked into a two-year contract they didn’t remember signing and had to keep paying for extra numbers and users they didn’t need. Other users mention they’re unable to cancel at all and continue to be charged every month. Do I need a landline for RingCentral? No. RingCentral is a communications solution that lets you make and receive VoIP calls using the internet and one of your devices. Is RingCentral free or paid? RingCentral is a paid business phone system. It doesn’t offer a free plan. However, it does offer a free trial to teams with fewer than six users. Does RingCentral pricing include hardware? No. RingCentral’s per-user plans cover the calling service and software only. Desk phones, headsets, and conference-room equipment are sold or rented separately. RingCentral supports compatible devices from brands like Poly and Yealink. Does RingCentral offer non-profit discounts? According to RingCentral’s website, it doesn’t offer special discounts to non-profits. However, you can check with their sales team whether they have an offer for non-profits. How does Quo’s pricing compare to RingCentral if my team needs unlimited texting and shared numbers? Quo includes unlimited business texting in the US and Canada on all its pricing plans. RingCentral requires a high-volume SMS add-on, and you’ll still need to pay $0.01 per message. Quo also includes shared phone numbers for texting, so teams can work together to solve customer issues. In contrast, RingCentral requires an additional add-on for shared texting that costs $25 per user per month. What hidden fees should I be aware of with RingCentral pricing? RingCentral pricing can increase quickly as your team’s usage grows. For example, texting and toll-free calling are capped on every plan. This can make it harder to predict monthly costs as your team scales and conversations pick up.

body_text: Future of Learning August 05, 2026 Greg Forbes SHARE Share this item with Copy this link https://plc.pearson.com/en-GB/news-and-insights/blogs/pearson-crowns-2026-microsoft-office-specialist-and-adobe-certified Key takeaways Finalists from around the world competed in 2026 Certiport Microsoft Office Specialist (MOS) and Adobe Certified Professional (ACP) World Championships in California. Competitors demonstrated in-demand digital, creative and productivity skills using technologies widely used in education and the workplace. Employer-recognised certifications help learners prove their skills and prepare for an AI-enabled economy. How do certifications help learners prepare for careers? Certiport , a Pearson Professional Assessments business, hosted the MOS and ACP World Championships. The event drew more than 190 finalists from 46 countries to Anaheim, California, to compete in disciplines like Microsoft Word, Excel ® and Powerpoint ®; and Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign. To reach the global finals, learners aged 13 to 22 first earned professional certifications and won national competitions in their home countries. Their achievements are impressive, but the bigger story is what they represent. Across industries, employers are looking for evidence that candidates can apply knowledge in practical settings. Digital skills, creativity, communication and problem-solving are becoming increasingly important as technology reshapes the workplace. Certifications help learners demonstrate those capabilities with credentials that employers recognise and trust. Microsoft winners celebrate their success Pearson's Certiport Microsoft Office Specialist World Champions: Liang Xinzhi, Macao, China, Microsoft PowerPoint™ (Office 2019) Reem El Shafii, Lebanon, Microsoft Word (Office 2019) Zhong Tin Kin, Macao, China, Microsoft Excel™ (Office 2019) Nguyen Mai Chi, Vietnam, Microsoft Excel™ (Microsoft 365 Apps) Sio Keng Nim, Macao, China, Microsoft Word (Microsoft 365 Apps) Santiago Matteus Dardón Pinzón, Guatemala, Microsoft PowerPoint™ (Microsoft 365 Apps) Why are employer-recognised credentials important in an AI economy? The rise of AI is accelerating demand for people who can combine technical expertise with adaptability and critical thinking. Certifications help learners build and validate those skills early, creating clearer pathways into higher education and employment. Arthur Valentine, President of Assessment and Qualifications at Pearson, said: "These students have not only earned valuable credentials, they have demonstrated the commitment, capability, and confidence needed to succeed in a fast-changing digital world. Their initiative and adaptability show exactly the kind of future-ready talent employers need. Professional certifications provide a trusted measure of skill level and capability, and these young people are already proving they can deliver." Adobe winners celebrate their success Pearson's Certiport Adobe Certified Professional World Champions: First Place: Lulu Emanuele, USA Second Place: Furtini Baldesin, Brazil Third Place: Muhammad Fawwaz Haiqal Bin Mohd Fuaad, Malaysia How is Pearson helping learners build career-ready skills? Across our qualifications, assessments, credentials and enterprise solutions, Pearson helps learners develop in-demand, employer-recognised skills so they can hit the ground running when they enter the workforce. The Certiport World Championships bring this to life. Participants demonstrate not only technical proficiency, but also the creativity, resilience and problem-solving skills that employers increasingly value. As employers continue to seek candidates with job-ready skills, qualifications and certifications that provide trusted evidence of what people know and can do will become even more important. The young people competing in Anaheim this year are proof of what can happen when learners invest in building those capabilities early. Congratulations to all participants, finalists and winners. Their success demonstrates the power of skills to unlock opportunity and help learners thrive as they embark on their careers and beyond. body_text: NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Today, Estée Lauder announces the launch of Glimmer , a new prestige fragrance created for a new generation of consumers. An amber floral fragrance with a gourmand twist, Glimmer transforms the power of everyday "glimmers” - small moments of joy, hope, and connection - into a sensorial fragrance experience designed to inspire optimism, foster community, and leave a lasting impression. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260727469772/en/ Hailee Steinfeld stars as the face of Glimmer Acclaimed actress and singer Hailee Steinfeld stars as the face of Glimmer. Rooted in the belief that one spark can ignite many, the campaign positions Hailee and her singing voice as catalysts for the joy, optimism, and connection that are at the heart of Glimmer. “Hailee is the embodiment of what Glimmer represents; she is confident, has a contagious sense of joy, and understands the power of connecting with her community,” said Justin Boxford, Global Brand President, Estée Lauder. “Consumers have grown up with Hailee and have followed her journey from a young actress to an accomplished multi-hyphenate artist and cultural force. Founded by Estée Lauder, beauty pioneer and one of the world’s first female entrepreneurs, the brand today continues her legacy of creating the most innovative, sophisticated, high-performance skin care and makeup products and iconic fragrances – all infused with a deep understanding of women’s needs and desires.
